facts.text: Founded in 1670 by Jean‑Baptiste Le Gardeur, son of seigneur Pierre Le Gardeur, Repentigny began as a small agricultural settlement.
Repentigny sits north of Montreal on the lower L'Assomption River, right where the river meets the Saint Lawrence.
The town was the western terminus of the historic Chemin du Roy, a road that once stretched eastward to Quebec City.
In 2002, Repentigny merged with the neighboring city of Le Gardeur, forming the modern municipality we see today.
Every late August, Repentigny hosts the National Bank Junior Tennis Internationals of Canada, the country’s largest junior tennis event.
During winter, the Festival de Feu et de Glace lights up Repentigny with fire and ice displays that draw visitors from across the region.
